name: Spanish Seafood Paella

components.name: Seafood Paella
steps: Check live mussels; discard cracked ones that do not close when tapped. Clean and debeard before cooking.
Warm fish stock and infuse 0.2 g saffron. Heat 45 ml oil in a broad paella pan and briefly sauté 300 g squid.
Add grated tomato, 10 g minced garlic and 2 g paprika; cook until the sofrito thickens.
Stir in 320 g dry rice to coat. Pour in approximately 1000 ml hot stock; reserve the remainder to adjust according to pan and rice.
Cook uncovered at a steady simmer. After rice has begun to absorb liquid, position peeled shrimp and mussels across the top.
Cook until rice is tender, shrimp opaque and mussels open. Discard unopened mussels; rest 5 minutes.
Garnish with parsley and lemon. This dish is best served fresh; do not promise ideal paella texture after freezing.

notes: Draft — needs Mirna review: not kitchen-tested yet; macros and cooked yields are estimates.
Seafood-only version without chorizo or chicken. The source supplies precisely weighed shrimp, squid, mussels and rice. Mussel weight includes shells and is not counted as 100% edible in estimates.
Storing & reheating: Paella is best on cooking day; rice texture and shellfish quality decline after refrigeration. If prepped, refrigerate up to 1-2 days and reheat thoroughly.
Freezer: T RECOMMENDED: texture loses quality

Refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour above 32°C) in shallow containers at 4°C or colder and follow the shorter seafood limit above. Cook fish to 63°C, shrimp and shellfish until opaque and firm (mussels must open), and reheat to at least 74°C.

flags.shelfLife: Paella — best on cooking day; fridge 1-2 days at most, don't freeze.

foodSafety: Refrigerate perishables promptly in shallow containers: within 2 hours after cooking, or within 1 hour if the air temperature is above 32 C.
Store at 4 C or colder. General cooked-leftover limit: 3-4 days; for delicate seafood recipes follow any shorter specific limit above.
Freeze later-week portions promptly, if this recipe is flagged freezer-suitable; thaw in refrigerator, not on a kitchen counter.
For fish, target a safe cooked internal temperature of 63 C; shrimp and shellfish should be cooked until opaque / firm, and mussels must open during cooking.
Reheat leftovers thoroughly to 74 C, avoiding repeated reheating and cooling cycles.
Cooked rice requires rapid chilling, appropriate cold storage and thorough reheating. Rice left warm for a prolonged period is not made safe by reheating.
Shellfish, fish, soy, dairy, wheat, egg, nuts and pork vary by recipe; verify allergens and dietary restrictions before importing.
